source: Piper et al. (2003) The BrainIT group: concept and core dataset definition
text: This is the minimum minute by minute monitoring data required for inclusion in the BrainIT Database and include: Heart Rate, Respiration Rate, Mean Arterial Pressure, mean ICP, SaO2 and Temperature.

classes.label: Monitoring Data
classes.definition: Continuously recorded physiological measurements collected from bedside monitors.

classes.label: Core Monitoring Parameter
classes.evidence: minimum minute by minute monitoring data required
classes.definition: A mandatory physiological variable collected at minimum once per minute.

classes.label: Heart Rate
classes.definition: The number of cardiac contractions per minute, a core physiological monitoring parameter in neuro-ICU.

classes.label: Respiration Rate
classes.definition: The number of breaths per minute, measured via impedance plethysmography or ventilator.

classes.label: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
classes.definition: The average arterial blood pressure during a cardiac cycle, a key haemodynamic parameter.

classes.label: Intracranial Pressure (ICP)
classes.definition: The pressure inside the cranium, continuously monitored to detect intracranial hypertension in TBI patients.

classes.label: SaO2
classes.definition: Arterial oxygen saturation measured by pulse oximetry, indicating blood oxygenation levels.

classes.label: Temperature
classes.definition: Core body temperature measured at rectal, oesophageal, bladder, or skin sites.

source: Moss et al. (2013) Trusting Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Medical Data
text: Each observation is evaluated by a data quality assessment. Errors are classified as either a Possible Error (PoE), where a reading is outside an acceptable range, or a Probable Error (PrE), where the error is confirmed by clinical context. A PrE may be reclassified as PoE if contextualised by a medical disorder such as sepsis or hypertension, or by a recent treatment such as noradrenaline or adrenaline.

classes.definition: A catecholamine drug used for haemodynamic support in critical care.
